patterns.name: WORD_WIDTH_TYPEDEF
patterns.why: a fixed width is asserted onto `long`, whose width is platform-dependent (the exact MD5 defect)

patterns.name: WORD_WIDTH_ASSUMPTION
patterns.why: code states or tests an assumption about a 32-bit word

patterns.name: ENDIANNESS
patterns.why: byte order is handled explicitly; correctness may depend on which branch is taken

patterns.name: ALIGNMENT_CAST
patterns.why: a byte buffer is reinterpreted as a wider type; unaligned access is UB on some targets

patterns.name: SIGNED_CHAR
patterns.why: plain `char` signedness differs between platforms (ARM vs x86)

patterns.name: TIME_32BIT
patterns.why: time held in a platform-width integer; Y2038 / representation change

patterns.name: INT_OVERFLOW_RELIANCE
patterns.why: behaviour depends on signed-overflow semantics, which are undefined in C

note: Presence of a pattern is NOT a defect. ENDIANNESS especially usually means the authors handled byte order deliberately. Only a two-world TEST can show correctness actually depends on the environment; this census only says where to look.
